function: Per-antenna transmit power allocation inside the BS ZF or hybrid precoder, analog or discrete, maximising long-term energy efficiency under QoS constraints (pp. 4, 7-9).
system: Single-cell downlink, 64-antenna UPA BS, 4 users with 16 antennas each, ZF digital or hybrid precoding, hardware impairments, no RIS, band not stated (pp. 3, 11).
method: Reinforcement learning: REDQ (Q-function ensemble) with an action coding scheme for discrete power levels, trained online on Markov channel states (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh fading with path loss and shadowing over a finite-state Markov chain; hybrid case uses a single-path array-response channel; no standard model or dataset (pp. 3, 5-6).
test_conditions: Online training and evaluation in one simulated environment (reward versus training steps); user number varied 2 to 20 with scaled power budget, policy reuse not stated (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Learned only: SAC, TD3, DDPG (reward versus training steps); no non-learned allocation compared; analog versus discrete and with versus without HWI are variants (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Reward (energy efficiency over QoS deviation, with penalties), energy efficiency, average per-antenna and total power versus training steps and users; operation counts (pp. 8, 11-14).
complexity: Complexity orders, e.g. O(Ne J |B| M Nd K^2) for fully digital analog allocation; operation counts 3.28e8 (digital) and 4.09e7 (hybrid), Table II (pp. 10-11, 14).
q1_support: p. 5: "We model the channel as a Rayleigh fading channel, where"; a custom simulated model (hybrid case: single-path array response, p. 6), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "of users is K = 4 and the number of antennas of the BS"; one simulated setup trained online, and the sweep of K (p. 13, Fig. 10) rescales the power budget, with no reuse of a trained policy stated.
q3_support: p. 12: "algorithms including SAC, TD3, and DDPG as baselines"; only learned baselines on reward versus training steps, with no non-learned power allocation compared.
q4_support: p. 14: "Table II compares the computational complexities of various PA schemes"; complexity orders such as O(Ne J |B| M Nd K^2) on p. 10 and operation counts 3.28e8 and 4.09e7 in Table II.
q5_support: p. 11: "In simulations, we consider a scenario where the number"; self-simulated setup, with no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Area 3: the REDQ agent chooses the per-antenna power matrix P that enters the ZF precoder (p. 4) and the hybrid precoder (pp. 5, 9); the precoders themselves are fixed designs. q3 fails because only RL baselines (SAC, TD3, DDPG) are compared, and the comparison plots reward over training steps. q4 is met by complexity orders and operation counts (Table II, p. 14).
